thin.what is missing: Pre-1456 outline is Steiermark only. March of Styria page: Ottokar III (1129-1164) 'extended his influence down the Mur river into the Mark an der Sann territory' and acquired 'large territories along the Savinja river down to the Windic March'; 1042/43 conquests 'up to Pitten and the Leitha river'. Duchy page: 'acquisition and re-acquisition' of the Celje estates, duchy in 'northern Slovenia'. Against: Lower Styria page ('Lower Styrian lands were ruled by several immediate (reichsfrei) dynasties like the Counts of Celje', 'not incorporated by the Habsburg dukes until the 15th century'). Settle it: either add Lower Styria (at least the Sann/Savinja lands) and Pitten to the 1180 outline with a 1341 loss of the County of Cilli to county-of-celje (Counts of Celje page: 'immediate counts (Reichsgrafen) from 1341') before the 1456 regain, or keep Steiermark-only and cite both pages in the keyframe note.

The 45 km Maribor disc (25 cells, 18 outside Steiermark) is centred on the Drava plain, catches one Prekmurje cell and one Croatian Krapina-Zagorje cell, and misses 4 of the 7 cells of the Savinja municipalities (Celje, Zalec, Velenje, Lasko...) where the counts sat ('on the Sann (Savinja) river in Lower Styria', Counts of Celje page). Use {"region": "Lower Styria"} once the gazetteer has it, or a union of Savinjska and Podravska municipalities plus the Styrian part of Pomurska west of the Mur.

1254 is a partition entered as a rename: the Ottokar II page has Ottokar 'yield large parts of Styria to Bela' (undated); the part kept by Ottokar/Austria (Traungau, Pitten) and its loss are not drawn.

Zones empty although the author's note quotes ground taken in Styria (Matthias Corvinus page: 1479 'the fortresses of the Archbishopric in ... Styria', 1481 'the town of Mautern in Styria'); Cliopatria puts all Styria under Hungary 1487-1491; no occupation event or contest zone.
One keyframe for 462 years; the 1918-1919 partition (southern third of Lower Styria with Maribor to the SCS state) is undated and has no loss event.
Gap 1246-1254 (no holder) and no rulers after Ferdinand II (1637).
